content: Final safety sweep: confirm no secret material leaked into my logs.

Merge node complete. Summary:

**Merge** (main workspace, branch `fix/stage-0-acceptance-blockers`, `26a604a` → `2355382`), four `--no-ff` merges in order B1 → host-key → relay-confirm → provider-profile. Two conflicts, both in `ji-remote-bootstrap`, resolved as a capability union rather than one side overwriting the other:

- [RemoteOrchestration.java](/E:/Projects/Code/AI/Ji/ji-java/products/ji-remote-bootstrap/src/main/java/io/github/diodeme/ji/remote/RemoteOrchestration.java:283) now does one `scanner.scan(...)` returning `SshHostKeyScanner.Scan`, then the B1 terminal re-check, then the kex-aware empty check. `javap` on the built jar confirms both `isTerminal` guards and the `Scan` consumers survive compilation.
- [RemoteOrchestrationTest.java](/E:/Projects/Code/AI/Ji/ji-java/products/ji-remote-bootstrap/src/test/java/io/github/diodeme/ji/remote/RemoteOrchestrationTest.java:484) merged the `FakeRunner` ssh-keyscan branch into one that keeps B1's `holdScan` blocking hooks and the host-key exit-code/stderr fields; 13 original tests grew to 15, all green.

No new state, second state machine, or fallback branch was introduced.

**Verification, all freshly run on the merged tree (`2355382`)**

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `./gradlew check --offline --rerun-tasks --no-build-cache` ×2 | BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 163/163 tasks executed each (2m58s / 2m50s) |
| `pnpm --filter @ji/web-app test` | 31 files / 217 tests |
| `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` / production build | exit 0 / `✓ built in 4.05s` |
| `pnpm check:generated` / `buf lint protocol/relay` | 122 files reproducible / exit 0 |
| `node scripts/run-stage5-real-topology.mjs` | `STAGE5_REAL_TOPOLOGY_OK` |
| Real Host install → authorized Ubuntu target | 8/8 PASS, `succeeded`, gate fingerprint `ssh-ed25519 SHA256:xdlm0…`, `restPort=36183` |
| Provider round-trip (`dialogue-roundtrip.mjs`) | `RESULT=ALL_PASS`, assistant replied `ACK` |
| Merged scan probe vs real target | `keys=3`; Windows OpenSSH candidate exits 1 with `unsupported KEX`, Git's succeeds — the fallback really is what produced the keys |

The four BLOCKERs therefore hold simultaneously: B1 terminal guard (plus `OrchestrationEndpointTest` 3/3 repeats — that case was the load-sensitive flake pre-merge), B2 scan resilience, B3 confirmation decoupling, B4 projection round-trip.

**Notable honest caveats recorded in the report** (183-line [merge-report.md](<//export/user/.gold-band/projects/e-projects-code-ai-ji--a40d4379/tasks/task-025/runs/run-001/rounds/round-001/nodes/ai-dynamic/attempt-001/dynamic/nodes/d18-wave2-fix-merge/attempt-001/attachments/merge-report.md>)): the B1 `stateSequenceAfterCancel` observation is sampled, not deterministic; the audit-race test's load sensitivity was not re-proven under three-way sibling concurrency; the installer still cannot overwrite an existing `versions/<version>` with different content; the §11.7 gate covers only "confirmation holds without a token"; and `dialogue-acceptance.mjs`'s `500`s are its own stale-revision noise — it reproduces the branch's after-fix log line-for-line, so §11.1 rests on the round-trip driver.

**Cleanup**: removed the three `%TEMP%\ji-d18-*` directories this run created, no leftover ssh/scp processes, no listeners on 4175/4176; remote `ji-host.service` verified `active`. Docker, Caddy and non-JI services untouched. Attachment-wide scan for the four `.env` secret values and PEM key blocks returned no matches.
